from pydantic_cli import run_and_exit, DefaultConfig", "replace": "from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict
from pydantic_cli import run_and_exit", "explanation": "Pydantic V2 uses a `model_config` dict set via `ConfigDict` instead of a nested `Config` class (migration.md#changes-to-config). `ConfigDict` is added to the pydantic import. `DefaultConfig` is removed from the import because the nested class that subclassed it is being replaced and no other use remains in this file."}, {"finding_ids": ["pydantic_cli/examples/simple_with_json_config.py:28:config-class"], "search": "class Opts(BaseModel):
    class Config(DefaultConfig):
        CLI_JSON_KEY = "json-training"
        CLI_JSON_ENABLE = True", "replace": "class Opts(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(CLI_JSON_KEY="json-training", CLI_JSON_ENABLE=True)", "explanation": "Replaces the deprecated V1 `class Config` with `model_config = ConfigDict(...)` (migration.md#changes-to-config). The keys and values are unchanged."}], "notes": "The config-class finding is addressed. Two caveats for review. (1) The old nested class inherited from DefaultConfig, and the new model_config does not. Any other DefaultConfig attributes the CLI relies on are no longer inherited here. This is only safe if pydantic_cli/core.py reads these keys from model_config rather than from a nested Config class, or if DefaultConfig adds nothing beyond these keys. I did not inspect DefaultConfig because it is outside this file. (2) CLI_JSON_KEY and CLI_JSON_ENABLE are not standard ConfigDict keys. Pydantic V2 stores unknown keys in the dict without error, but type checkers will flag them, and the library must read them from model_config. The module docstring mentions BaseModel.Config; I left it as prose."}
